name: TSMC’s 16FF FinFET process
description: TSMC developed its original 16 nm FinFET foundry process and produced working customer silicon, including a HiSilicon processor designed for networking equipment.

date.label: November 2013
date.basis: TSMC’s October 2014 earnings call dates the start of original 16FF risk production to the preceding November.

events.statement: TSMC began risk production on its original 16FF process.
events.scope: Pilot manufacturing ahead of high-volume production.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 5, C. C. Wei’s remarks on the 16 nm ramp
evidence.supports: Separates the variants and dates base 16FF risk production to November 2013.

date.label: 25 September 2014
date.basis: The date is the release date of the public disclosure.

events.statement: TSMC announced that it had made a functioning 32-core HiSilicon networking processor with 16FF logic dies.
events.scope: A customer networking processor. TSMC reports a separate 28 nm I/O die in the package.

evidence.supports: Identifies the application, logic process, and working customer silicon.

earliest_record.rationale: The foundry dates the distinct 16FF risk-production milestone to November 2013.
